subject: health
unitTitle: Staying Safe at Home, Outside, and Online
title: Explicit model: emergency help and calling 911
essentialQuestion: How do I spot a hazard early and choose the safest next step?
materials: paper or a printed checklist for a home safety walk
a properly fitted helmet if wheels are discussed
keyPoints: In the United States, call 911 for a real emergency: a fire, someone badly hurt, someone who cannot breathe, or a crime happening now.
Say what happened, where you are including the full address, and your name.
Do not hang up until told to.
Learn your home address and a guardian's phone number by heart, and know where the phone is.
Calling 911 as a joke is never safe, because it takes help away from someone who needs it.
Non-emergencies — a scraped knee, a lost pet, a broken window — go to a trusted adult, not to 911.
privacySafeScenario: A neighbor has fallen and cannot get up or reach a phone. Is this a 911 call? Say out loud exactly what you would tell the operator.
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about emergency help and calling 911 to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: State the most important rule or fact about emergency help and calling 911 in your own words.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about emergency help and calling 911.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: A safety walk may be done by an adult with the learner directing from a seated position, by spoken description with no photographs taken, or entirely through a floor-plan drawing. No learner is required to reach, lift, or test any hazard.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about emergency help and calling 911 under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, walk the home fire escape route and agree the outside meeting place. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
